You are an adversarial security auditor pentesting the Nxeon platform's AUTHENTICATION, SESSION, and ADMIN/RBAC surfaces. Read-only code audit, no edits, no destructive actions. Codebase: /opt/nxeon-wt-annual (git worktree, Next.js 15 App Router + Prisma; auth via NextAuth-style; server actions).

GOAL: take over an account, escalate to admin, or access admin-only actions as a normal user.

SCOPE:
- **Auth**: login, password hashing, password reset (token generation/expiry/reuse — lib/actions-account.ts reset flow), email verification, 2FA/TOTP (bypass? backup codes?), session cookie security (httpOnly/secure/sameSite, signing), account lockout/rate-limiting on login + reset. Can you forge or fixate a session? Predict a reset token?
- **RBAC / admin**: lib/rbac.ts (requireArea), how admin server actions are guarded (grep app/admin + lib for requireAdmin/requireArea). Find any admin/staff action or admin API route or admin page that is NOT properly guarded — a normal authenticated user reaching an admin capability. Area-gating bypass (SUPPORT reaching ADMIN-only). Privilege escalation via a self-service action that sets role/permissions.
- **Impersonation**: admins can impersonate customers — can an impersonating admin do things they shouldn't (assertNotImpersonating coverage)? Can a normal user trigger impersonation?
- **IDOR across the app**: server actions/API routes that take an id (serverId, accountId, invoiceId, ticketId, domainId, teamId, mailboxId) — do they ALL verify the caller owns/can-access it, or can you pass someone else's id? Team/organization membership checks.
- **API tokens**: lib/ API token auth — scope, leakage, whether a token can exceed its owner's permissions.

For EACH finding: file:line, concrete exploit (attacker steps → unauthorized access), severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MED/LOW), fix. Be a skeptic — trace the actual guard on each sensitive action. An unguarded admin action or a working IDOR is CRITICAL. Return markdown: findings most-severe first (file:line + exploit + fix), then a "verified guarded" list. Report to orchestrator, findings only. Do NOT edit files.

/**
 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
 *
 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
 */
export type Area =
  | "overview"
  | "analytics"
  | "clients"
  | "support"
  | "fleet"
  | "billing"
  | "platform";

/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
  platform: ["ADMIN"],
};

export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
}

/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
}

 * literal IPs; empty = no restriction. Fails OPEN (allows) when the list has no
 * parseable entries or the requester IP can't be determined, so a bad value can
 * never lock every admin out — only an exact match is ever enforced.
 * Returns true when access should be REFUSED.
 */
async function adminIpBlocked(): Promise<boolean> {
  const raw = await getSetting("allowed_admin_ips", "");
  const entries = raw.split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  if (entries.length === 0) return false; // no restriction configured
  const valid = entries.filter(isPlainIp);
  if (valid.length === 0) {

    return false; // malformed -> fail open
  }

  // Trust nginx's X-Real-IP ($remote_addr), which the client cannot forge. Fall
  // back to the LAST X-Forwarded-For hop (the one our proxy appended), never the
  // client-supplied leftmost entry.
  const xff = (hdrs.get("x-forwarded-for") ?? "").split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  const ip = hdrs.get("x-real-ip")?.trim() || xff[xff.length - 1] || "";
  if (!ip) {
    console.warn("[admin-ip] could not determine requester IP; failing open");
    return false;

92	 * may they spend/provision? Separated from the DB so the whole policy — the

97	  user: Pick<VerifiableUser, "emailVerifiedAt" | "createdAt">,
98	  mailWorks: boolean,

101	  if (isGrandfathered(user)) return true;

180	  const raw = randomBytes(32).toString("base64url");
181	  await db.emailVerificationToken.create({

192	export type ConsumeResult = "ok" | "already" | "invalid" | "expired" | "stale";

196	 *

198	 * NOT an error: people click the same link twice, and mail security scanners
199	 * fetch links before the recipient ever sees them. Both outcomes end with a

201	 *
202	 * `stale` means the token was minted for an address the account no longer uses —
203	 * verifying it would assert control of the wrong mailbox.
204	 */
205	export async function consumeVerificationToken(rawToken: string): Promise<ConsumeResult> {
206	  if (!rawToken) return "invalid";
207	  const row = await db.emailVerificationToken.findUnique({ where: { tokenHash: hashToken(rawToken) } });
208	  if (!row) return "invalid";
209	  const user = await db.user.findUnique({ where: { id: row.userId } });
210	  if (!user) return "invalid";
211	  if (normalizeEmail(user.email) !== normalizeEmail(row.email)) return "stale";
212	  if (user.emailVerifiedAt) return "already";
213	  if (row.usedAt) return "invalid";
214	  if (row.expiresAt < new Date()) return "expired";
215	
216	  const now = new Date();
217	  await db.$transaction([
218	    db.user.update({ where: { id: user.id }, data: { emailVerifiedAt: now } }),
219	    db.emailVerificationToken.update({ where: { id: row.id }, data: { usedAt: now } }),

5	 * `"use server"` — and in such a file EVERY export becomes a network-callable

15	 * A post-login destination that is guaranteed to be on this site, or null.
16	 *
17	 * An unvalidated `?next=` on a login form is an open redirect, which is a
18	 * phishing primitive: an attacker sends `…/login?next=https://evil.test/`, the
19	 * victim signs in on the REAL site and is handed to the attacker's page, already
20	 * primed to trust it. So this allows exactly one shape — a single-slash absolute
21	 * path — and discards everything else rather than trying to sanitise it:
22	 *
23	 *   "/dashboard/migrate"  -> kept
24	 *   "//evil.test/x"       -> rejected (protocol-relative; the browser treats it
25	 *                            as a host, and `startsWith("/")` alone lets it past)
26	 *   "https://evil.test"   -> rejected
27	 *   "/\\evil.test"        -> rejected (backslash is a slash to some parsers)
28	 *   "dashboard"           -> rejected (relative)
29	 */
30	export function safeNext(raw: FormDataEntryValue | null): string | null {
31	  const s = typeof raw === "string" ? raw.trim() : "";
32	  if (!s || s.length > 512) return null;
33	  if (!s.startsWith("/")) return null;
34	  if (s.startsWith("//") || s.startsWith("/\\")) return null;
35	  if (/[\x00-\x1f]/.test(s)) return null;
36	  return s;

I've completed a thorough audit of the authentication, session, RBAC/admin, impersonation, IDOR, and API-token surfaces — covering the core auth library, all `[id]`/`[serverId]` API routes, the OAuth and terminal/console token flows, and every server-action file (via two parallel deep scans plus manual verification of the linchpin guards `resolveMailbox`, `ownedServer`, `requireArea`, `verifyTotpForUser`, `assertSessionToken`).

## Summary

This is a heavily hardened worktree. Nearly every sensitive file carries comments documenting a prior vulnerability of exactly the classes in scope (2FA oracle, cross-tenant mail takeover, impersonation-token promotion, timing enumeration, coupon races) and how it was closed. I could not find a working account-takeover, privilege-escalation, or IDOR. Below is the one real (low-severity) gap, then the verified-guarded evidence.

## Findings

### LOW — Session cookie `Secure` flag gated behind an extra env var, inconsistent with the impersonation cookie
`lib/auth.ts:27` (session + `nxeon_authed` flag) vs `lib/auth.ts:194` (impersonation cookie).

- Session cookie: `secure = process.env.NODE_ENV === "production" && process.env.COOKIE_SECURE === "1"`
- Impersonation cookie: `secure = process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"`

The *primary* session cookie (the credential that grants full account access) only gets the `Secure` attribute if an **additional** `COOKIE_SECURE=1` env var is set, while the shorter-lived impersonation grant is `Secure` in production unconditionally. A production deploy that forgets `COOKIE_SECURE=1` therefore ships the session cookie — and the `nxeon_authed` flag — without `Secure`, so any plaintext-HTTP request to the domain (a downgrade, an `http://` link, an active MITM) can leak the session token, enabling hijacking.

- Exploit: attacker on-path induces one HTTP request to the app host; the browser attaches the non-`Secure` `nxeon_session` JWT in cleartext; attacker replays it as a valid session.
- Mitigants that lower severity: `httpOnly` + `sameSite=lax` are always set, and a correctly configured deploy sets the flag. This is the one cookie policy in the file with no explanatory comment justifying the discrepancy.
- Fix: gate the session cookie's `secure` on `NODE_ENV === "production"` alone (matching the impersonation cookie), or document why the split exists; default `COOKIE_SECURE` to on in production rather than off.

No CRITICAL or HIGH issues were identified.

## Verified guarded (traced, not just named)

- **Login / password** (`lib/actions.ts`): unconditional bcrypt against a dummy hash on missing accounts (no timing oracle); rate-limit keyed on trustworthy `clientIp` (not client-supplied XFF); identical error text; suspended check.
- **2FA** (`lib/totp-verify.ts`, `lib/totp.ts`, `lib/actions-2fa.ts`): TOTP steps single-use via `claimOnce` (RFC-6238 replay closed); backup codes consumed with a compare-and-swap `updateMany`; `verifyTotpForUser` deliberately kept out of any `"use server"` module so it is not a network-callable brute-force oracle; enrollment blocked while impersonating.
- **Password reset** (`lib/actions-account.ts`): `randomBytes(32)` token, sha256-hashed at rest, 1h expiry, `usedAt` single-use, `sessionVersion` bump; email+IP throttle; detached send + always-success response (no enumeration).
- **Session/impersonation** (`lib/auth.ts`): `assertSessionToken` rejects promotion of an `imp` grant into a session; `realUser` enforces `sessionVersion` + suspension; `currentUser` re-checks target suspended/ADMIN at use time; `requireAdmin` (built on `currentUser`) refuses to act while impersonating; admin layout redirects on active impersonation; `assertNotImpersonating` covers spend/reveal paths (wallet top-up, renew, resize, card, NxCloud password reveal/reset/terminate, etc.).
- **RBAC** (`lib/rbac.ts`): area→role map, `requireArea` uses `realUser` (impersonation-ignoring), unknown admin hrefs default to ADMIN-only; role changes only via `setUserRole` (`requireAdmin`, can't self-edit); no non-admin path writes `User.role`/`balance`/`isFree`. Admin portal additionally host-gated, IP-allowlisted, and optional staff-2FA enforced.
- **IDOR across app** (both deep scans + manual): every `[id]` API route and server action resolves ownership (`row.userId === user.id || ADMIN`) or an area gate before touching a resource — servers, disk, metrics, console (VNC), terminal, files, hosting FS, invoices, domains/DNS export, backups (with archive-tenancy re-check), volumes, databases, SSL, mail (`resolveMailbox` scopes to `subscription.userId`; company mailboxes staff-only), calendar, tokens, GDPR export, gift codes, tickets. Deletes use scoped `deleteMany({ where: { id, userId }})`. `/api/search` and `/api/metrics` scope non-admin queries to `userId`.
- **API tokens** (`lib/api-auth.ts`): sha256-stored, `revoked`/`expiresAt`/suspended honored; empty scopes fail **closed** to read-only; single `authorizeApiRequest` entry point + a test tripwire; the one token route (`/api/v1/servers`) enforces `servers:read` and filters to `userId`.
- **OAuth** (`app/api/auth/google/callback`): CSRF `state` vs httpOnly cookie; requires Google `email_verified` before linking; unusable random password hash for new accounts.
- **Open redirect**: `safeNext` allows only single-slash absolute paths (rejects `//`, `/\`, absolute, control chars); used by login and OAuth.
- **Terminal/console tokens**: short-lived JWE (A256GCM), salt-separated keys, ownership re-checked at the minting route and again in the PTY backend (`terminal-server/index.ts` re-loads the server and asserts `server.userId === claims.userId`).
- **Teams** (`lib/actions-teams.ts`, `lib/team-guard.ts`): membership mutations verify actor's `canAdministerOrg` role in the *target* org (derived from the membership, not client-supplied); invites are encrypted (JWE) consent tokens bound to one email and re-verified at accept; OWNER role never assignable via invite; the write-only `Membership.areas` fake-control was removed rather than left half-wired.

Report ends. No edits were made; all paths above are absolute under `/opt/nxeon-wt-annual`.
